Copper
KOP-er
noun
Hebrew nechosheth (H5178) — the same word translated brass, since modern brass (copper-zinc) did not exist in biblical times; ancient copper and bronze (copper-tin alloy) are what the Hebrew text actually names. Distinguished from "brass" only in modern context; in Scripture the two are the same metal.

📖 Biblical Definition

Copper is what the biblical Hebrew nechosheth ALMOST ALWAYS names — pure copper or bronze (copper-tin alloy), not the modern brass of zinc-copper alloy which postdates the biblical era. Where older English translations say "brass," modern accurate translations often say "bronze" or "copper." Job 28:2 says "Brass is molten out of the stone" — Hebrew nechosheth, copper. Deuteronomy 8:9 promises Israel a good land "a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills thou mayest dig brass" — copper. Solomon's Edomite copper mines at Timna (modern southern Israel) produced enormous quantities of the metal for the temple work (1 Kings 7:13-47). Two notable copper men in Scripture: Hiram of Tyre, the master craftsman who cast all the bronze work for Solomon's temple (1 Kings 7:13-14; 2 Chr 4:11-18), "filled with wisdom, and understanding, and cunning to work all works in brass"; and Alexander the coppersmith, who did Paul "much evil" (2 Tim 4:14) — possibly a metalworker whose silver-craftsman analog stirred up trouble in Ephesus over the gospel's threat to idol-making trades (Acts 19:23-41). Copper's biblical role is mostly subsumed under "brass" theology (judgment, altar, serpent), but the distinct copper note is valuable: it is the metal of WORKMANSHIP, of the craftsman's skill in the tabernacle and temple, of the visible labor by which God's house was made beautiful.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The reddish-brown ductile metal (Cu); what biblical Hebrew nechosheth almost always names (translated brass in older English); the metal of temple craftsmanship.

expand to see more

COPPER, noun. A reddish-brown ductile metal (Cu); the parent of bronze (copper-tin alloy) and modern brass (copper-zinc alloy).

In Scripture, the Hebrew nechosheth (translated brass in older English) most accurately names copper or its alloys. The metal of Job 28:2; the mineral wealth of the promised land (Deut 8:9); Solomon's Edomite mines (1 Kings 7:13-47); the craft of Hiram of Tyre and Alexander the coppersmith.

📖 Key Scripture

Deuteronomy 8:9 — "A land wherein thou shalt eat bread without scarceness, thou shalt not lack any thing in it; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills thou mayest dig brass."

1 Kings 7:14 — "He was a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in brass: and he was filled with wisdom, and understanding, and cunning to work all works in brass."

Job 28:2 — "Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass is molten out of the stone."

2 Timothy 4:14 — "Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: the Lord reward him according to his works."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Copper is corrupted when modern translations bury the distinction between copper, bronze, and the modern zinc-alloy brass (using "brass" anachronistically), or when the temple-craftsmanship theology of Hiram is severed from the larger biblical pattern of Spirit-given skill in beautifying God's house.

expand to see more

Translation anachronism. The English word "brass" originally covered copper and its alloys broadly; modern usage restricts brass to the copper-zinc alloy that did not exist in biblical times. Older translations like the KJV use "brass" for what the Hebrew text actually names as copper or bronze. Modern translations have variously corrected this (sometimes to "bronze," sometimes to "copper") — but the consistent theology of the metal is what matters more than the exact modern crystallographic identification.

Craftsmanship-theology loss. Hiram of Tyre is described as "filled with wisdom, and understanding, and cunning to work all works in brass" (1 Kings 7:14) — language directly echoing Bezalel and Aholiab in Exodus 31:1-11 ("I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship") who built the tabernacle. God's house is built by Spirit-given craftsmen working in copper/bronze/gold/silver/wood. To miss this is to flatten the biblical theology of work: skilled workmanship is a Spirit-given gift, and the beauty of God's dwelling depends on craftsmen whose hands the Spirit has filled.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew nechosheth (H5178) — copper, bronze, or brass; the metal of temple craftsmanship and the promised land's mineral wealth.
